A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Statistical Collusion by Collectives on Learning Platforms. Their main text, equations, seven figures, Table 1, algorithms, and Appendices A–F are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations on synthetic vehicle-evaluation data, including observed test-set success for signal planting and unplanting in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and observed success curves, including feature-label planting, adaptive unplanting, and feature-only planting in Figures 1, 3, and 5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Appendix B retain the same planting, adaptive unplanting, and erasure procedures. Renaming the estimation-subset size from n_est to n_e does not change the algorithm or data partition.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic vehicle dataset, four evaluation labels, SUV signal, and planting/unplanting scenarios. Appendix C retains the same feature-only planting evaluation; no dataset, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains the naive strategies targeting Good, Average, and Poor, while Figure 4 retains the feature-label and feature-only bounds from Hardt et al. (2023). The newly cited Ben-Dov et al. work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains sampling without replacement from 3,000,000 instances, default training/test sizes of 1,000,000/100,000, delta = 0.05, and epsilon = 0. The population-size and estimation-subset sweeps, transformations, and success metrics also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The population-size sensitivity in Figure 2, estimation-subset and strategy comparisons in Figure 3, and bound-sensitivity analyses in Appendix E are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same theoretical confidence parameters and Hoeffding estimation terms. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, empirical error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–7 retain the same curves, and Table 1 retains all sample counts. Numerical findings also remain unchanged, including approximately 10% collective size suggested by the unplanting bound versus approximately 3% observed in practice.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorems 3.3, 3.5, 3.7, and 3.9, and the proofs and infinite-data results in Appendices D–F are unchanged. The estimation-subset rename and correction of a stray probability hat are notation edits without revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and discussion retain the same claims about finite-sample collective inference, signal unplanting, tighter infinite-data bounds, staircase behavior, and the importance of absolute collective size.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain substantively unchanged, including finite feature spaces, identically distributed participants, conservative guarantees, and impractical erasure bounds in Appendix E.5. The new Impact Statement repeats the existing societal motivation.

D1.justification: Section 3.2.1 and Appendix A change the stated repository from GauthierE/statistical-collusion to GauthierE/statistical-algorithmic-action. This revises access information; the PDFs document no accompanying implementation or experimental-setting change.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ben-Dov et al. (2024), The Role of Learning Algorithms in Collective Action, with a sentence acknowledging how learning algorithms shape collective success. The broader positioning and comparisons with Hardt et al. remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammatical and notation corrections, clarifies the relationship between N and n at fixed n/N, renames n_est to n_e, and adds a short Impact Statement. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML-style two-column main text, with different typography, title and affiliation placement, running headers, and resized or repositioned figures. Appendices are reflowed, and Figure 3's caption explicitly defines G/A/P. The underlying displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through the corrected probability notation in Section 3.1, clearer fixed-ratio explanation in Section 4.1, and explicit legend abbreviations in Figure 3. The additional collective-action citation improves context. Methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and limitations are preserved, so the overall gain is limited to presentation and contextual completeness.
